name: Anwar Ibrahim
_note: M2 cohort expansion (key figures): Prime Minister and Finance Minister since the unity government formed (24 Nov 2022). Objective spine (A5, C1) plus a provisional Layer B pass on file; below ranking validity pending the remaining objective dimensions and an independent Layer B panel. Layer B (Editorial Panel) is a SINGLE-CODER provisional first-coder pass (coderScores length 1): each score is recorded and cited but NOT scored, normalized, or ranked, per methodology.validity.minCodersToScore=3. Citations verified to exist via search; article full text was not opened (environment fetch restriction), so facts rest on cross-outlet-corroborated search summaries and require primary-source reconfirmation before any independent panel finalizes the score.

metrics.justification: Factual status only, not a re-litigation of guilt. Convicted of corruption / abuse of power (Kuala Lumpur High Court, 14 Apr 1999, six-year sentence) and, in a separate matter, of an offence affirmed by the Federal Court on 10 Feb 2015; granted a FULL royal pardon by the Yang di-Pertuan Agong on the advice of the Pardons Board on 16 May 2018 and released the same day. No charge or anti-corruption matter against him personally is of record within the current term. Scored under the published "pardoned" status (0.7).

citation.title: Malaysia: Anwar Ibrahim released after getting full pardon

metrics.justification: Shapley-Shubik power index of the leader's coalition (Pakatan Harapan) among the seven blocs of the 222-seat Dewan Rakyat (GE15, simple-majority quota 112), computed by scripts/compute-pivotality.mjs. PH=0.4048, PN=BN=0.2214, GPS=0.0714. Coalition-level because per-party tallies carry a 1-2 seat contradiction immaterial to the index. Descriptive structural weight, not a merit score.

metrics.justification: Crisis handling as PM/Finance Minister: the ringgit fell about 3.5% in early 2024 (he called it "concerning" on 23 Feb 2024 while citing strong fundamentals) and recovered to a 14-year high by 4 Aug 2024, though substantially on external rate factors and BNM action; on 1 Dec 2024 he allocated an extra RM50m to flood-hit Kelantan and Terengganu. Adequate, externally-aided responses with mixed attribution (anchor 2).

citation.title: Ringgit at its strongest in 14 years, says Anwar

metrics.justification: Championed reforms delivered and operative, primary-sourced: targeted diesel subsidy retargeting effective 10 Jun 2024 (price to RM3.35/litre, projected ~RM4b/year saved); the Public Finance and Fiscal Responsibility Act 2023 (Act 850) in force 1 Jan 2024; and mandatory e-invoicing phased from 1 Aug 2024. RON95 retargeting was delayed past mid-2025 (see B4). Multiple hard reforms gazetted and operative (anchor 4).

citation.title: Government Implements Targeted Diesel Subsidy For Peninsular Malaysia Effective 10 June 2024

metrics.justification: Institution-building: signed the 16 Dec 2022 confidence-and-supply MOU with BN, GPS and GRS (148 of 222 seats; confidence motion passed 19 Dec 2022) and introduced Prime Minister's Question Time and the Fiscal Responsibility Act. Independent reviews (BERSIH 2023, ISEAS 2024) credit these but flag that the promised PM/Finance-Minister separation and AG / public-prosecutor split were not delivered. Real but partial (anchor 3).

citation.title: Parties sign MoU backing Anwar, unity government

metrics.justification: The RON95 targeted subsidy, repeatedly promised for mid-2025, was announced delayed on 21 Jul 2025 "due to further tweaks in mechanism" and reframed as a RM1.99/litre price cut on 23 Jul 2025. The timing reversal was acknowledged with a stated reason, but largely via a minister and paired with a more favourable reframing rather than a direct on-record account (anchor 2).

citation.title: Targeted RON95 subsidy rollout delayed due to further tweaks in mechanism, says Fahmi
